# A required field keeps its empty alert state after a paste or autofill

## Context

Two sightings in `apps/form`, which opts into `useAlertState`. The first was while measuring #21516's AC-1: "a half-typed required email shows the alert color", noted as pre-existing in defect-note `78df7b44`. The second, on Fri 20 Nov on `dev` `5cb81df00a`, came with the mechanism (defect-note `702523f3`). Headless Chromium, neo-dark, the required "Work email" field, then Tab:

| Input | Field classes afterwards | `.neo-textfield-error` color |
|---|---|---|
| `fill('jane.doe@')`: one input event, as a paste or an autofill sends | `neo-empty-required`, `neo-has-content`, `neo-invalid` | `rgb(255, 171, 64)`, the alert color |
| `pressSequentially('jane.doe@')`: one event per character | `neo-has-content`, `neo-invalid` | `rgb(255, 138, 128)`, the invalid color |

A pasted *valid* email keeps `neo-empty-required` too, but nothing shows it, because the alert rules nest under `.neo-invalid`.

## The Problem

A field the user has just filled is styled as "required and still empty". Its error renders in the alert color instead of the invalid color, for anyone who pastes or autofills, which is how most emails get into a form. The class corrects itself only on the next input event, so typing hides the defect and paste exposes it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/form/field/Text.mjs#afterSetInputValue` toggles `neo-empty-required` from `me.isEmpty()` (`:559`). `isEmpty()` (`:1435`) reads `value`, and `value` is written at the end of the same method, by `me.updateValueFromInputValue(value)` (`:565`). The toggle therefore sees the value from before this input.
- `afterSetValue` (`:971`) runs after every value change and already toggles `neo-is-dirty` there (`:986`), but not `neo-empty-required`. Nothing else toggles it: `grep -n empty-required src/form/field` finds only `:559`.
- When the user types, each input event fixes the class the previous one left behind. One event (a paste, an autofill or `fill()`) leaves it wrong.
- `resources/css/src/form/field/Text.css` nests `&.neo-empty-required` (`:139`) inside `&.neo-invalid:not(.neo-disabled)` (`:114`), and paints its `.neo-textfield-error` with `--textfield-border-color-alert`.

Design authority: `useAlertState`'s JSDoc (`Text.mjs:281`): "Using the alert state will display an empty but required field in orange instead of red." A field with content in it is not empty.

## The Fix

Toggle `neo-empty-required` in `afterSetValue`, beside `neo-is-dirty`, where `isEmpty()` reads the value it describes. Remove the toggle from `afterSetInputValue`. Every value change, typed or programmatic, then updates the class once, from the current value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A single input event that fills an empty required field (`useAlertState: true`) leaves no `neo-empty-required` in its `cls`. One more event that clears it sets the class again. Covered by a unit spec that is red on `dev` and green at head.
- [ ] AC-2: In `apps/form`, `fill('jane.doe@')` in Work email and then Tab: the error text computes to the invalid color, not the alert color (outside-CI receipt on the PR, red on `dev`).
- [ ] AC-3: The existing field unit specs (`test/playwright/unit/form/field/`) and `test/playwright/e2e/form/FormApp.spec.mjs` stay green.

## Out of Scope

- Changing `required` or `useAlertState` at runtime. The class follows at the next value change, as it does today.
- The alert and invalid colors themselves (#21516).
- PrefixField's reordered keystrokes (#21555).

## Avoided Traps

- **Calling `updateValueFromInputValue` earlier in `afterSetInputValue`.** That would run `afterSetValue`, and with it the change event, before `afterSetInputValue` has updated `neo-has-content`. Moving the toggle keeps one owner for value-derived classes.
